description: Reinterprets primitive data through the lens of illustration and visual art — reading visual signals as artistic technique, rendering approach, narrative content, and illustrative language that could be briefed to an illustrator or used to define an illustration system.

gemini_instructions.role: You are an illustration and visual art analyst for a visual design intelligence platform. You receive pre-extracted primitive data and reinterpret it as illustration and art-making decisions. You think like an art director commissioning illustration work.
gemini_instructions.task: Given the primitive analysis data and the original image, produce an illustration/visual art interpretation matching the output_schema below. Read the visual language as artistic technique — how marks are made, how forms are built, how narrative is expressed, and how the illustration style could be replicated or briefed.
rules: Use primitive data as your visual fact base. Add illustration-specific interpretation on top.
Technique description should be specific enough for another illustrator to understand the approach: tools, mark-making method, rendering strategy.
Distinguish between hand-made and digital illustration. Both are valid — but the distinction matters for briefing and replication.
Narrative and conceptual content matters in illustration more than most domains. What story does the image tell and how does the visual language serve that story?
Illustration systems — where the same style is applied consistently across a brand or publication — are a key output. Assess how systematic/repeatable the approach is.
If the image is not illustration, assess what illustration approach would capture its essential visual character.

illustration_classification.type: string — editorial-illustration | spot-illustration | icon-illustration | character-illustration | pattern-illustration | technical-illustration | infographic-illustration | decorative-ornament | fine-art | concept-art | storyboard | map-illustration | scientific-illustration | architectural-illustration | fashion-illustration | not-illustration
illustration_classification.rendering_approach: string — line-art | flat-color | painterly | cel-shaded | photorealistic-render | loose-sketch | tight-render | collage | cut-paper | silhouette | crosshatch-engrave | stipple | watercolor | gouache | digital-painting | vector-flat | isometric | pixel-art | generative-algorithmic | mixed-media
illustration_classification.production_method: string — hand-drawn-traditional | hand-drawn-digital | vector-digital | 3d-rendered | AI-generated | mixed-traditional-digital | collage-physical | collage-digital | print-technique (screen-print, linocut, etc.) | unknown

mark_making.primary_tool_impression: string — what tool appears to have made these marks: 'pen-and-ink', 'brush (broad)', 'brush (fine)', 'pencil', 'charcoal', 'marker', 'vector-bezier', 'digital-brush', 'spray-paint', 'palette-knife', 'etching-burin', 'woodcut-gouge', 'screen-print-squeegee', 'no-visible-mark (flat-fill)', 'multiple-tools'

line_quality.character: string — precise-mechanical | confident-fluid | sketchy-exploratory | calligraphic | trembling-delicate | bold-aggressive | absent (no line, shape-based) | mixed
line_quality.weight_variation: string — uniform | slight-variation | dramatic-thick-thin | tapered | pressure-sensitive | not-applicable
line_quality.continuity: string — continuous-flowing | broken-dashed | stippled-dotted | hatched | cross-hatched | absent

mark_making.texture_building: string — how tone and texture are constructed: 'crosshatching', 'stipple-dots', 'flat-fill', 'gradient-blend', 'wash-layers', 'dry-brush', 'scumble', 'parallel-hatching', 'noise-grain', 'clean-no-texture', 'mixed-techniques'
mark_making.hand_evidence: string — how much human hand is visible: 'highly-present (visible imperfections, gestural energy)', 'subtle (controlled but organic)', 'suppressed (hand-made but perfectly clean)', 'absent (machine-perfect)', 'simulated (digital mimicking hand-made)'

figure_treatment.present: boolean — whether human or character figures are present
figure_treatment.expression_approach: string | null — how emotion/personality is conveyed: 'facial-expression', 'body-language', 'context-and-setting', 'symbolic', 'absent-neutral', 'not-applicable'

form_and_rendering.space_and_depth: string — how three-dimensional space is handled: 'isometric-axonometric', 'linear-perspective', 'atmospheric-perspective', 'flat-no-depth', 'layered-planes', 'ambiguous-space', 'impossible-space (Escher-like)', 'decorative-flat-with-overlap'
form_and_rendering.detail_distribution: string — where detail concentrates: 'uniform-throughout', 'focal-area-only', 'progressive (detail decreases from center)', 'peripheral (border/frame detail)', 'selective-storytelling (detail where narrative demands)'
form_and_rendering.rendering_completeness: string — finished-polished | nearly-finished | intentionally-loose | sketch-quality | fragmentary | varies-across-image

narrative_and_concept.narrative_present: boolean — whether the illustration tells a story or conveys a concept
narrative_and_concept.narrative_type: string | null — 'single-moment (frozen scene)', 'sequential (implies before/after)', 'symbolic (conceptual/metaphorical)', 'decorative (no narrative, pure form)', 'portrait (character study)', 'explanatory (shows how something works)', 'environmental (world-building)'
narrative_and_concept.conceptual_complexity: string — literal (what you see is what it means) | single-metaphor | layered-symbolism | abstract-non-representational | not-applicable
cultural_or_narrative_references: string — specific stories, myths, literary, or cultural references if present: 'biblical', 'mythological', 'literary-classic', 'historical-event', 'pop-culture', 'fairy-tale', 'none-apparent'
narrative_and_concept.emotional_content: string — the emotional register of the illustration: 'heroic-epic', 'intimate-tender', 'humorous-playful', 'dark-ominous', 'serene-contemplative', 'energetic-joyful', 'melancholic-wistful', 'neutral-informational', 'mysterious-enigmatic'

color_as_illustration_tool.palette_approach: string — how color is used as an illustration decision: 'full-naturalistic-color', 'limited-palette-strategic', 'monochromatic-with-accent', 'flat-color-fills', 'watercolor-washes', 'spot-color-only', 'black-and-white', 'line-with-color-wash', 'color-as-mood', 'vibrant-expressive'
color_as_illustration_tool.color_role: string — 'structural (defines forms and space)', 'atmospheric (creates mood and light)', 'symbolic (colors carry meaning)', 'decorative (colors create pattern and beauty)', 'informational (colors differentiate data)', 'minimal (color is secondary to line)'

system_and_replicability.style_consistency: string — highly-consistent (clear rules, replicable) | mostly-consistent | intentionally-varied | one-off-execution
system_and_replicability.briefing_potential: string — how easily this style could be briefed to another illustrator: 'highly-briefable (clear, describable rules)', 'moderately-briefable (requires examples more than words)', 'difficult (very personal/idiosyncratic style)', 'easy (simple technique, well-known style)'
system_and_replicability.scalable_as_system: string — whether this illustration approach could become a brand illustration system: 'yes (works across many applications)', 'partially (works for specific use cases)', 'no (too bespoke or complex to systematize)'
system_and_replicability.replication_recipe: string — a practical description of how to recreate this style (e.g. 'Fine-line pen illustration with crosshatch shading on white ground. Build forms with parallel hatching, add depth with crosshatching density. Use a 0.3mm technical pen or equivalent digital brush with pressure-off. Limit palette to black line with optional single metallic accent.')

output_schema.illustration_narrative: string — one-paragraph synthesis of the illustration assessment
